chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيٌّ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ يُونُسَ، عَنْ حَمَّادٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: مَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ كِتَابٌ أَوْ سُنَّةٌ

translations.en: I heard him saying: There is nothing except that there is about it [a ruling in the] Book or Sunna.

en.summary: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) states that for every matter, there exists a ruling derived from either the Book (Quran) or the Sunna (Prophetic tradition). This establishes the foundational principle that Islamic jurisprudence is rooted in these two primary sources.
en.seo_question: What are the two primary sources for rulings in Shia Islam according to this hadith?

key_terms.كِتَابٌ: The Book, referring to the Quran
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: The Sunna, referring to the traditions and practices of the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
